File:03 ALBERT EINSTEIN.ogg.author: Radio Universidad Nacional de La Plata
File:03 ALBERT EINSTEIN.ogg.description:
Voice of Albert Einstein recorded by the Radio of the National University of La Plata. Text:

"Ladies (coughs) and gentlemen, Our age is proud of the progress it has made in men's intellectual development. The search and striving for truth and knowledge is one of the highest of men's qualities - though often the pride is most loudly voiced by those who strives the least, and certainly, we should take care not to make the intellect our goal. It has of course powerful muscles but no personality. It cannot lead, it can only serve, and it is not fastidious in its choice of a leader. This characteristic is reflected in the qualities of its priests, the intellectuals. The intellect has a sharp eye for methods and tools, but is blind to ends and values. So it is no wonder that this fatal blindness is handed on from old to young and today involves a whole generation."
Women's voice: "Albert Einstein, mil noveciento(s) cuarenta tres" (Spanish?, 1943)
Text of an address by Albert Einstein

On April 11, 1943, United Jewish Appeal organized a fundraiser and a broadcast appeal featuring several noteworthy personalities including this short address by Professor Albert Einstein, himself a Jew and a refugee who had managed to escape Hitler’s Germany.

Albert Einstein – Address For United Jewish Appeal – With Asst. Sec. of State Joseph C. Grew – April 11, 1943 – Gordon Skene Sound Collection, pastdaily.com Albert Einstein Has A Word Or Two About Truth, Knowledge And Values – 1943 – Past Daily Reference Room

File:A Teen's Story about Cross-Country.author: Be Here Main Street
File:A Teen's Story about Cross-Country.description:
This story was collected in conjunction with the national traveling exhibition "Hometown Team: How Sports Shape America" by the Museum on Main Street program at the Smithsonian Institution. It is part of the "Be Here: Main Street" collection, intended to capture Americans' stories about their neighborhoods, waterways, towns, traditions, and personal experiences. Learn more about the project and the terms and conditions. #bHereMainSt

"When I first started running, I could not make it past one mile without spilling my guts all over the pavement. After a little bit of training with the cross-country team, I got the hang of it. I wasn’t the best runner, but at least I could go 3.1 miles without stopping. Then, I made the best decision of my life. I joined the cross-country team. And, with the whole school and town supporting us, it felt great. Then on September 1, race day arrived. I was sitting with the Junior Varsity when Mr. Favinger came up to us and said, 'It’s time boys.' Immediately, my heart started pounding so hard that it felt like it would bust out of my chest. We walked to the line, and my legs were shaking and my heart was racing 100 mph. Looking to my team’s right, I saw a large number of Cozad supporters. At the sight of this, my worries went away.

Then the gun went off. I heard a large band, and I just took off. The pack started forming. There were three main packs—front, middle, and the back of the pack. Jack, Abraham, Zackery, and I feel into the middle pack. With each step, Jack and I sped up, but with each step more pain came. We both felt rotten but we sped up anyway because you can’t feel any worse. Then after 22 minutes of agony, we finished. I have changed a lot as a runner. I went from not being able to run 2 miles to being able to run 13 miles in a single run. Running has become a part of my life here in Cozad, and Cozad fans are into it as much as I am. All the supporters are what make each and every runner go faster."
File:A Teen's Story about Cross-Country.categories: Youth|Cozad, Nebraska|Cross country running|Self-published work|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation|Audio files about sports|Audio files about running|Be Here: Main Street

File:17-creatures.flac.author: Сomplex Numbers
File:17-creatures.flac.description:
Audio text:

<tapping on the test tube>

DOCTOR: So that's what your pets look like.

Little Mermaid: Careful, don't blow...

DOCTOR: And they're like this... so they fashioned this light bulb here??

<tapping on the light bulb>

Doctor: With metal and glass parts? How to mold this here, is there a vacuum inside or something?

The Little Mermaid: Yes.

DOCTOR: Listen... yes... Three-dimensional printers, of course, in our time, no one will be surprised. But to light the bulb…

The second Prince: <laughter> I'm not really surprised by anything anymore. People can only watch from the side and wait for their fate.

DOCTOR: Optimistic, yes! Is it possible with their help, for example, to make a young human body and transplant someone's brain there? Well, for example, some old man…

The Little Mermaid: You can even superhuman. It is only necessary to program a detailed design, and it will slowly assemble ... And so, my little animals can do almost everything.

Doctor. Aren't you afraid, so to speak, of a machine uprising?

The Little Mermaid: No, they're almost brainless. We need computers to control them. And this is just the problem. One computer fully controls only a small number of them, and if some macrostructure is assembled by atoms, it is easier to shoot yourself right away.

DOCTOR: Yes, well, in general, it's clear. Okay, in general, do not forget that we are meeting tomorrow in the IAPU dining room, I found new victims for you there. One student will come tomorrow and another the day after tomorrow.

File:\"Motor Boat Rag\" by Henry W. Gaul.author: Henry W. Gaul
File:\"Motor Boat Rag\" by Henry W. Gaul.description:
Original listing and sheet music here: https://musescore.com/user/36482158/scores/12780610?from=youtube_share 
How come every rag that originates anywhere near Cincinnati turns out to be "a good rag"? This obscure rag from nearby Newport, Kentucky is no exception. Published by Tropwen Music Co. in Newport in 1911. It's the only findable work by musician Henry William Gaul, who lived from 1895 to 1947 and is buried in Cincinnati, Ohio.

Original score source was from Walter Cosand at this link (copy/paste entire URL if needed): http://waltercosand.com/CosandScores/Composers%20E-K/Gaul , %20Henry%20W/Gaul-Motor_Boat_Rag.pdf

This is a reproduction of the original score with a few amendments. Added repeat bars to the Trio (because it's a nice trio); changed the note durations at measures 13 and 46 so they make sense; added various missing accidentals in the B and C strains, most notably to all the Bs in measure 60; deleted the left-hand Es in measure 68.
File:\"Motor Boat Rag\" by Henry W. Gaul.categories: Media from YouTube|PD-old-75-expired|CC-PD-Mark|Uploaded with video2commons|PD-old missing SDC copyright status

File:\"The Japanese Sandman\", Fox-Trot.description: Welte-Mignon (Licensee) reproducing piano roll #6012. Issued September 1920. Pianist/arranger J. Milton Delcamp lived in Norristown, Pennsylvania most of his life. He led a theatre orhestra when only in his teens. He graduated from the Combs Conservatory in Philadelphia. In 1918 he joined Adam J. Carroll in recording piano rolls for the Unisolo and De Luxe roll companies in Philadelphia. After Carroll moved to New York, Delcamp joined him in making rolls for the Republic Player Roll Company in 1919. This led to arranging rolls for the Welte-Mignon (Licensee) company in 1920. The very first issued "Licensee" roll was Delcamp's "Stop, Look, Listen To The Music of the Band." Shortly thereafter Carroll and Delcamp both switched allegiance to a competing company, AMPICO (American Piano Company) where they perfected their roll-making skills. Delcamp was also heard on radio. An item in the New York Times (Mar 11, 1928) said: "Sentimental music and popular ballads will be the contribution on WJZ to the auditors of an eleven station network Thursday night at 8:30 o'clock. J. Milton Delcamp, pianist, will be the featured artist." His last roll for AMPICO was made in 1928. By 1930 Delcamp and his wife, Mabel (nee Miller), had returned to 1345 DeKalb Street in Norristown, PA with their four daughters. In the April, 1930 census he gave his occupation as music director. It is likely his brother was Robert Delcamp, organist at St. Thomas Church, 5th Ave at 53rd Street. J. Milton Delcamp's piano rolls are widely collected by members of the Automatic Musical Instrument Collectors Association (AMICA) in the U.S.

File:\"Pekin Rag\", by Harry W. Martin (.author: Harry W. Martin
File:\"Pekin Rag\", by Harry W. Martin (.description:
Original listing and sheet music here: https://musescore.com/user/36482158/scores/19420072?from=youtube_share 
"As Played by Martin's Military Band". This is a great rag, by an otherwise unknown composer, but it had a rough beginning. The printer/engraver, Groene Music Pub. Co. of Cincinnati, botched the score pretty badly with a bunch of errors. Rather than go into that, suffice to say that this is a corrected version that allows you to hear it as was intended, and it's well worth hearing.

According to JohnJ1995, the rag is named after the Pekin Theater in Cincinnati, a relative of the famous Pekin Theater in Chicago which spawned an earlier "Pekin Rag" by Joe Jordan in 1904: https://musescore.com/user/36482158/scores/10151053

Pekin also refers to the largest city in China, now called Beijing in English.

Original score source was from the Let's Rag website at this link: https://lets-rag.com/pekin-rag This is a reproduction of the original score with many corrections.

Thank you to the patient listener on YouTube who suggested this rag.

File:49 Deepak Chander Ledwani Recounts.author: EngProff
File:49 Deepak Chander Ledwani Recounts.description: Deepak Chander Ledwani is a 65-year-old retired Life Insurance Corporation (LIC) Development Officer. He currently oversees a family-run plastic furniture business in Ulhasnagar, managed by his sons. His family's roots trace back to the post-Partition migration; his grandfather settled in the region and sold wholesale vegetables in Kalyan. His father initially worked in Bombay manufacturing mixer-grinders before starting a small-scale electronic and plastic parts manufacturing unit from their home in Ulhasnagar. Ledwani was born and raised in the city, receiving his education and building his career there, grounding his perspective deeply in the local history and community dynamics. Ledwani spent his formative years in "C-Block," which was characterized by larger plots compared to other places. Living conditions in the barracks were communal and deeply intertwined. Homes featured rudimentary wooden doors and cement sheet roofing, which made summers intensely hot. Residents frequently adapted their living spaces to accommodate growing families without seeking official municipality permissions such as converting kitchens into bathrooms and extending rooms into adjacent boundary spaces. The socioeconomic makeup of the barracks was diverse, encompassing day laborers, government employees, and small business owners operating out of their homes (such as neighboring biscuit factories). Ledwani vividly recalls the sensory details of the barracks, particularly the distinct Sindhi calls of street vendors selling everyday items like Kuneha Bih (lotus roots) and Dal Moong. Despite an enduring affection for Ulhasnagar, describing a deep "sik ain prem" (love and longing) for his home soil, Ledwani is candid about the city's infrastructural stagnation. He notes that while roads have widened, civic sense regarding waste management and parking remains poor, and the city still lacks high-quality, affordable healthcare facilities. The proliferation of illegal buildings and the subsequent redevelopment crises forced him to relocate to Kalyan. He observes that while physical structures are transforming from barracks into modern towers, the systemic issues of poor drainage and chaotic urban planning persist. Nevertheless, he emphasizes that Ulhasnagar remains a vital cultural and commercial hub, drawing people from as far as Bombay for wedding shopping and specialized goods, underscoring the strong, enduring community ties that define the city.
File:49 Deepak Chander Ledwani Recounts.categories: Self-published work|Barracks of Ulhasnagar: An Oral History of a Refugee City

File:74 Nimmi Mohan Guwalani Recounts He.author: EngProff
File:74 Nimmi Mohan Guwalani Recounts He.description: Nimmi Mohan Guwalani, a 63-year-old former railway employee and natural therapist, reflects on her family’s post-Partition journey and the historical evolution of Ulhasnagar. Born and raised in the Central Hospital Quarters in Ulhasnagar, Nimmi shares a detailed biographical account of her family’s roots and resilience. Her mother worked as a nurse in the Central Hospital after migrating from an affluent background in Pakistan, while her father was a railway employee whose mother was an active freedom fighter. Nimmi highlights her parents' staunch support for their daughters’ education despite prevailing societal resistance against educating women within the community at the time. This encouragement enabled her sister, Rani Khattwan, to achieve exceptional academic success, going on to work as a senior scientist at the Nehru Planetarium, undertake advanced studies at NASA in astro-physics, and later hold vice-presidential roles at Intel, IBM, and Microsoft. Focusing on the unique personal and historical fabric of Ulhasnagar, Nimmi vividly describes growing up in the hospital quarters during the post-Partition resettlement era. The quarters, originally built during the British period with sturdy masonry and spacious layouts for senior staff, functioned as a close-knit, multicultural joint family where Maharashtrian, Gujarati, and Sindhi families lived in close harmony. She fondly recalls a time defined by deep communal bonds, open playgrounds, mutual assistance, and simple living without modern amenities like televisions or refrigerators. However, she contrasts this cherished heritage with the modern decay of Ulhasnagar, expressing sorrow over the loss of its historical barracks, the replacement of open green spaces with unregulated concrete structures, and the rampant proliferation of unsafe, illegal buildings. She recounts the distressing 2019 collapse of a neighbouring building, which forced her family to evacuate, highlighting the lack of government support, poor infrastructure, and civic apathy facing residents today. Through her personal memory and critique, the audio presents a poignant historical narrative of refugee resilience, community solidarity, and the urban decline of Ulhasnagar’s historic living quarters.
File:74 Nimmi Mohan Guwalani Recounts He.categories: Ulhasnagar|Self-published work|Barracks of Ulhasnagar: An Oral History of a Refugee City

File:79 Durupadi Hardasani Reflects on H.author: EngProff
File:79 Durupadi Hardasani Reflects on H.description: Durupadi Hardasani, a nearly seventy-year-old homemaker, shares her personal biography alongside her family’s post-Partition resettlement history in Ulhasnagar. Born in the Section 23 area of Ulhasnagar inside the Section 3 Government Hospital, Durupadi's lineage traces back to Khairpur in Sindh (now Pakistan). Her paternal grandfather, Rawaldas Hotramdas, was a prominent Luqman Hakim (traditional physician) whose renown was so great that the local area in Khairpur took on the name Luqman after him. Following Partition, her family migrated via ship, stopping briefly in Akbar (Thane) before obtaining land claims for a residence in Ulhasnagar. Her father worked as an electrical engineer at Power Cable in Vitthalwadi. Her maternal family, originating from Peer Goth near Karachi, owned a glucose biscuit factory and were associated with establishing the Shanti Prakash Ashram. Throughout her life as a homemaker, Durupadi has remained dedicated to community service, voluntarily teaching mathematics to underprivileged children and engaging in traditional Sindhi handiwork, including crochet, sewing, and aar (crochet/embroidery work). Durupadi provides a vivid description of her childhood home in Barrack Number 1027, Section 23 (OT 3, near Ashok Anil). The original barrack structure consisted of a simple four-room unit (kothi) allotted by the government, featuring narrow rear lanes and a spacious front plot that her family formally registered and acquired. Housing a large extended family of nearly forty members across four barrack rooms, the living arrangement was deeply communal. Early barrack living involved significant physical hardship; homes lacked internal bathrooms or toilets, requiring residents to fetch water manually and use shared, external municipal latrines. Due to her grandfather’s standing as a respected hakim, her family was granted municipal permission to construct an internal bathroom early on in 1960. Durupadi recalls unique physical features around the barracks, such as overhead Tata electrical cables running directly above the barrack roofs, which once led to a tragic incident when a young boy flying a kite was fatally shocked after his kite string made contact with the live wires. Reflecting on the evolution of Ulhasnagar, Durupadi contrasts the quiet, forested landscape of her youth with the dense, commercialised city of today. She remembers when the Gol Maidan area was an unpaved, dense jungle of thorns that felt so desolate and intimidating that residents hesitated to cross it after dark. She tracks how landmark sites transformed over the decades such as the Dussehra Ground becoming Indira Gandhi Market, open play spaces turning into gardens, and early single-screen theatres like Raju Talkies giving way to the Ashok Anil Theatre complex, alongside nearby military cantonment areas (chhawani) transitioning into commercial establishments like the Jawahar Hotel, Jawahar Theatre, and local multi-storey shopping complexes. She also recalls crossing the clean waters of the Ulhas River via a small wooden bridge (atim pul) near National School, lamenting how that once-vibrant river has degraded into a polluted drain. While acknowledging minor civic improvements in road block-paving and waste management, Durupadi expresses deep frustration over persistent infrastructural failures, including acute water shortages that force residents living on higher elevations to carry buckets of water from lower-lying homes. She notes that while living in barracks offered safety, open courtyards for traditional children's games (such as langdi and likachhupi), and close-knit neighbourly support, the transition to modern multi-storey buildings has created social stratification and reduced open community spaces. Durupadi highlights that Sindhi residents face systemic neglect regarding civic amenities compared to neighbouring areas, and she observes that families residing in barracks often face social stigma regarding matrimonial prospects. Despite these urban crises, she takes pride in her children's academic achievements – including her daughter topping CHM College in Sindhi – and calls for greater unity and mutual assistance within the Sindhi community.
File:79 Durupadi Hardasani Reflects on H.categories: Ulhasnagar|Self-published work|Barracks of Ulhasnagar: An Oral History of a Refugee City

File:80 Hansa Bablani Recounts Her Child.author: EngProff
File:80 Hansa Bablani Recounts Her Child.description: Hansa Bablani, a fifty-two-year-old assistant teacher, shares her personal biography alongside her reflections on the historical and civic evolution of Ulhasnagar. Born and raised in the township, Hansa’s paternal roots trace back to Partition, when her family fled landowning prosperity in Sindh to resettle in India. Following the traumatic loss of her extended family’s head in Pakistan, her family migrated via private ship and eventually settled at Nehru Chowk in Ulhasnagar through government property claim allocations. Her maternal family similarly rebuilt their lives, transitioning from operating horse-drawn carriages (tangas) to becoming major wholesale manufacturers of festive decorations in Indore. Growing up near Nehru Chowk, Hansa’s childhood was shaped by her family's local enterprises, including a cycle-rental business run by her father and an iconic lock-and-key shop run by her uncles, famously known across Section 5 as the Ghoongho Chabiwaro (a nickname derived from her uncle's hearing and speech impairment caused by an early childhood illness). In her detailed account of life in the post-Partition military barracks, Hansa highlights the distinct spatial layouts, social warmth, and architectural transformations of these refugee shelters. She describes her ancestral barrack as a linear home seamlessly integrated with their storefront, featuring wooden-plank beds, high display shelves, an inner kitchen, and an upper wooden loft built to house her extended joint family. While many neighbouring barracks were simple structures with unplastered walls, shared outdoor latrines, and basic kerosene stoves, Hansa’s family enjoyed early comforts such as scooters, televisions, and a rare refrigerator that served the wider area. Despite these material differences, she evokes a tight-knit "barrack culture" defined by shared meals, open doors, joint festival celebrations, and mutual reliance such as neighbours sharing water during severe municipal shortages. The sensory landscape of her childhood barracks was filled with the rumble of passing trucks near Nehru Chowk, the heavy metallic thud of brass mortars and pestles echoing through thin shared walls, and the lively chatter of open lanes. Reflecting on the broader transformation of Ulhasnagar, Hansa tracks its trajectory from a modest refugee settlement into a self-reliant manufacturing hub renowned for denim, gowns, and retail trade. However, her view of the city's modern infrastructure is tempered by concern over civic neglect and urban decay. She discusses the transition from single-storey barracks to modern multi-storey apartments, noting that while flats offer complete privacy, they lack the profound sense of community, open courtyards, and emotional security of the old barracks. She offers a sharp critique of the city's recurring housing crises, particularly the proliferation of unauthorised multi-storey buildings constructed with inferior materials, which have led to catastrophic structural collapses, displacement, and financial ruin for many families. Additionally, she addresses chronic civic issues such as severe road potholes, open drainage, traffic congestion, and the historical pollution of the once-pristine Ulhas River, where her family previously performed annual Ganesh immersions. Despite these persistent challenges, Hansa expresses an unshakeable emotional attachment to Ulhasnagar as both her birthplace and workplace, urging the Sindhi community to preserve their hard-working ethos, language, and cultural heritage.
File:80 Hansa Bablani Recounts Her Child.categories: Ulhasnagar|Self-published work|Barracks of Ulhasnagar: An Oral History of a Refugee City

File:99 Saju Jewani Reflects on Her Root.author: EngProff
File:99 Saju Jewani Reflects on Her Root.description:
Saju Jewani is a sixty-nine-year-old homemaker who was born and brought up in Ulhasnagar. Her family history reflects the typical diverse cottage trades that sustained early refugee households: her father operated a bakery in Camp 1, while her mother took up domestic tailoring work. Her paternal grandfather assisted at the bakery, alongside her grandmother who ground grain manually using a stone mill (jandu) and processed sugar candy (khand) at home, while her maternal grandparents ran a local tea shop. After completing her schooling, Devani married into a family where her husband worked in the corporate office of Britannia Biscuits. Today, she resides in Ulhasnagar in a joint household comprising her son, daughter-in-law, granddaughter, and herself, continuing to speak Sindhi as their primary household tongue.

In her recollection of Ulhasnagar’s housing landscape, Jewani provides a detailed spatial description of her family’s original allotment in the military-style barracks in Camp 1. The dwelling followed a sequential architectural layout, opening with an entrance kitchen space that led into an outer hall reminiscent of a verandah, which then opened into a large hall where the entire family slept together. Whilst a separate bathing enclosure was situated within the unit, the barracks lacked internal plumbing, obliging all households to rely on shared outdoor public latrines. Water was initially unavailable indoors; residents had to carry water in buckets from a common municipal tap installed in an outlying hall until neighbouring households collectively pooled their own funds to draw individual private pipelines into their homes. The domestic electrical setup was equally rudimentary, originally restricted to a single light bulb in the entire house, contrasting sharply with today's fully illuminated residences.

Jewani captures the unique social and emotional atmosphere of growing up in the barracks, portraying a tight-knit neighbourhood characterised by collective outdoor games, profound mutual affection, and an absence of industrial din. Her neighbouring households engaged in modest occupations, ranging from service employment to local grocery provisioning. A defining philosophical insight of her account emerges when reflecting on socioeconomic standing: she notes that while a well-to-do family in the neighbourhood ran a medical dispensary and possessed greater material amenities, true contentment and peace resided among the working-class families whose simple routines were free from anxiety. She firmly regards barrack life as safer and emotionally warmer than modern apartment complexes, where residents remain shut inside behind closed doors without knowing their neighbours.

Turning to the broader urban history and challenges of Ulhasnagar, Jewani reflects on the proliferation of illegal and poorly built multi-storey structures that have replaced many original barrack sites. She expresses constant apprehension regarding sudden structural collapses in Camp 3 and Camp 4, observing that when buildings crumble, displaced residents receive no government rehabilitation schemes and are left to reconstruct properties through private cooperative efforts and personal expense. She also highlights the ongoing deterioration of municipal roads, which remain broken and full of dug-up potholes that present a persistent danger of falls for pedestrians. Despite external stereotypes from outsiders who sometimes look down upon the township, Jewani regards Ulhasnagar as an indispensable sanctuary akin to Bombay, a self-contained, vibrant city that has provided abundant affection, community facilities, and public gardens, concluding with an earnest hope that the community will continue to progress and carry Ulhasnagar forward.

File:101 Heena Chotwani Explains Her Pre.author: EngProff
File:101 Heena Chotwani Explains Her Pre.description:
Heena Chotwani, a forty-four-year-old homemaker, was born and raised in Ulhasnagar, where her family roots and domestic life remain deeply anchored. Her mother was a homemaker, whilst her father initially worked in service at a printing press before establishing an independent family-run press specialising in wedding cards. She grew up in a household of five siblings, and today resides with her husband and mother-in-law in the OT section of Camp 3, balancing daily household routines with yoga and personal wellness.

Her childhood reflects the communal residential patterns typical of early Ulhasnagar. Her family initially resided in Camp 5, where five paternal uncles lived alongside one another in an extended family enclave centred around cattle sheds (kheer ja wada). As the family expanded and space became constrained, they relocated to a larger barrack near C.B. Chowk in Camp 2, which housed three to four rooms alongside an internal kitchen and washroom. While early barrack life lacked excessive consumer traffic and modern commercial noises, she notes that today’s barrack lanes are animated by daily street hawkers and vegetable vendors. Unlike many contemporary residents who perceive barracks as relics of poverty, Chotwani firmly views renovated barracks as inherently safer, more reliable, and far superior to modern multi-storey buildings. She emphasises that barracks offer regular, twice-daily municipal water supply and structural stability, avoiding the water shortages and structural anxieties chronic to poorly built local apartments.

Her critical perspective on Ulhasnagar’s urban built environment is rooted in direct observation of the city's housing crisis. Having witnessed the collapse of a building behind Regency Hall near Gol Maidan, which came down within an hour, causing total loss of possessions and devastating the residents, she expresses deep scepticism towards unregulated high-rise developments and stalled redevelopment initiatives. She notes that displaced families receive minimal institutional support and are left to fend for themselves in temporary rented flats. Concurrently, she traces the changing social fabric of Ulhasnagar from a quiet, cohesive, predominantly Sindhi settlement into a dense, multi-ethnic urban centre, pointing to the environmental degradation of the Ulhas River from industrial chemical effluents. Reflecting on the outside perception of Ulhasnagar, affectionately yet jokingly abbreviated as "USA" across Mumbai, she observes that while adults remain unaffected by the social stigma of living in barracks, younger generations increasingly experience linguistic and cultural alienation. In response, she concludes with an appeal to the Sindhi community for unity and urges parents to counter the dominance of English and Hindi by actively speaking, teaching, and passing down the Sindhi mother tongue to their children.
File:101 Heena Chotwani Explains Her Pre.categories: Self-published work|Barracks of Ulhasnagar: An Oral History of a Refugee City

File:Americanism (Franklin D. Roosevelt).author: Franklin Delano Roosevelt
File:Americanism (Franklin D. Roosevelt).description:
Franklin Delano Roosevelt, former Assistant Secretary of the Navy. Speaking of those who fell in battle, "To them we must write the binding finish: it shall not happen again. Americans demand: the crime of war shall cease."

Sound quality of recording is good.

Reverse side of disc is a music selection, not reproduced.

Believed to be take 1.

Inscribed in disc: 1-C-30.

This recording has been reproduced by the Library of Congress through the generosity of the family of Guy Golterman, and with the cooperation of CBS-Sony Records and the Recording Industry Association of America.

MEDIUM 1 sound disc : analog, 78 rpm ; 12 in.

TEXT

"Americanism"

Much has been said of late about good Americanism. It is right that it should have been said. And it is right that every chance should be seized to repeat the basic truths underlying our prosperity and our national existence itself. But it would be an unusual and much to be wished-for thing, if in the coming presentation of the issue a new note of fairness and generosity could be struck.

Littleness, meanness, falsehood, extreme partisanship: these are not in accord with the American spirit. I like to think that in this respect also we are moving forward. Let me be concrete. We have passed through a great war. An armed conflict which called forth every resource, every effort, on the part of the whole population. The war was won by Republicans as well as by Democrats. Men of all parties served in our armed forces. Men and women of all parties served the government at home. They strived honestly, as Americans, not as mere partisans. Republicans and Democrats alike worked in administrative positions, raised Liberty Loans, administered food control, toiled in munitions plants, built ships. The war was brought to a successful conclusion by a glorious common effort -- one which in the years to come will be a national pride.

I feel very certain that our children will come to regard our participation as memorable for the broad honor and honesty which marked it; for the absence of unfortunate scandal and for the splendid unity of action which extended to every portion of the nation. It would therefore not only serve little purpose, but would conform ill to our high standards, if any person should, in the heat of political rivalry, seek to manufacture political advantage out of a nationally conducted struggle.

We have seen things on too large a scale to listen at this date to trifles, or to believe in the adequacy of trifling men. It is that same vision of the higher outlook of national and individual life which will, I am sure, lead us to demand that the men who represent us in the affairs of our government shall be more than politicians; that they shall subordinate always the individual ambitions and the party advantage to the national good. In the long run, the true statements and the honestly forward-looking party will prevail.

Even if a nation entered the war for an ideal, so it has emerged from the war with the determination that this ideal shall not die. It is idle to pretend that the declaration of war of April 6, 1917 was a mere act of self-defense, or that the object of our participation was solely to defeat the military power of the central nations of Europe. We knew then as a nation, even as we know today, that success on land and sea could be but half a victory. The other half is not won yet. The cry of the French at Verdun, "They shall not pass" and the cheer of our own men in the Argonne, "We shall go through," these were essential glories, yet they are incomplete. To them we must write the binding finish -- it shall not occur again -- for America demands that the crime of war shall cease.�

Audio recording of a steam, gas-pumping engine made by Easton & Amos of London, and used by the South Metroplitan Gas Company, Old Kent Road, London from 1864 to the mid 1950s, and now at Thinktank, Birmingham.
The engine is started from cold. First, steam is allowed through the cylinders, their drain cocks open, to warm them. The flywheel is rotated by hand, to set the engine in motion, and the recording ends with the engine ticking over at low speed.

File:An interview with Margaret Killjoy.author: The Final Straw
File:An interview with Margaret Killjoy.description:
This week I had the opportunity to sit down with Margaret Killjoy to talk about her new EP called <a href="https://nomadicwarmachine.bandcamp.com/">Every Breath Our Last</a> out this October from her one woman project Nomadic War Machine. Margaret is a writer, musician, and anarchist based in Western North Carolina. We got to talk about a lot of things in this episode, including her new EP, what went into making it, Nomadic War Machine as a project in general, and her new anarchist fiction podcast called <a href="https://www.wewillrememberfreedom.com/">We Will Remember Freedom</a>.


This was a great conversation to have for me, and is a little bit of a different approach than what we usually do in that the conversation unfolded organically with little in the way of pre set prompts. I hope you will get a sense of sitting down at a kitchen table with two people who have known each other for some while, talking about stuff they would kind of normally talk about anyway, except it’s being recorded. I am also clearly not a music journalist, and that comes out, especially because I neglect to ask her about the political or social themes of her new EP. Give it a listen tho on any streaming platform!


Click on her <a href="https://www.patreon.com/margaretkilljoy">Patreon</a>

to support Margaret in her endeavors and to read more of her fiction.

This episode of the <a href="http://www.soleone.org/solecast/2018/9/7/w-margaret-killjoy-on-anarchist-sci-fi-the-cultural-war-prefiguration">Solecast</a> includes her reading a short story called The Northern Host (“nazis don’t go to Valhallah”), and an <a href="https://thefinalstrawradio.noblogs.org/post/2017/07/31/1645/">interview on TFS</a> where we talk about her then new book The Lamb Will

Slaughter the Lion.

FANG:



From their fundrazr page:


“The climate crisis, and ongoing destruction of landscapes and wildlife, are provoking a deepening sense of urgency in an increasing number of people. It can be a serious struggle to care for a world that is being plundered for profit, but there are more and more people turning their grief into resistance in defense of nature and other animals. From water protectors to pipeline protestors, and wildlife and caged animal defenders – good people who care for our world are standing up for all of us. Unfortunately taking such a stand can result in arrest,

court, jail, and prison time.

Background:

In 2016, <a href="https://nycabc.wordpress.com/fang/">project FANG</a> was established by the NYC ABC as a much-needed attempt to fill a gap in the ongoing support work for the growing number of eco and animal rights prisoners in the United States. The focus of project FANG funding is to help pay for prison visitation costs for friends and family of these prisoners.

Why are visits so important?

Visits from friends, family, and loved ones are repeatedly identified by prisoners as one of the most important life lines that exist for them. Without visits, the crushing isolation of life inside a prison becomes unbearable. However, visits can often be prohibitively expensive. Travel costs might include not only an expensive plane ticket, but also lodging, a rental car, and meals. These quickly add up to hundreds of dollars.

How you can help:

Currently, project FANG has committed funding of $5,000 per year, but due to the increase in eco and animal rights prisoners, and requests for visitation funding, we need to increase our available funds. With your support we are aiming to double the fund’s annual budget for 2019 and 2020 by raising $10,000. Can you help us reach our $10,000 goal?”

<a href="https://fundrazr.com/project_fang?ref=ab_d8c7xc_ab_5zRAZ25xVf75zRAZ25xVf7">To help support, please visit their fundrazr page!</a> Stay tuned to TFS for a possible interview with these folks in future, or visit our <a href="https://thefinalstrawradio.noblogs.org/post/2016/11/27/new-york-city-anarchist-black-cross/">archives</a> for a past interview with a founder of this project.

File:Bad Voltage 3\u00d704- They Call It.description:
Stuart Langridge, Jono Bacon, and Jeremy Garcia present Bad Voltage, in which we like egg. Also:


  • [00:02:38] And now, this: Famous rapper Jason Zed <a href='https://waxy.org/2020/04/jay-z-orders-deepfake-audio-parodies-off-youtube/'>orders deepfake parodies of his voice off YouTube</a>… Virginia spend time debating whether it’s ok to <a href='https://www.richmond.com/news/local/government-politics/bill-making-it-legal-to-drive-drunk-at-home-makes/article_26f295d3-7da9-52f5-950a-692f25a1c0d3.amp.html'>be drunk in your car while it’s in your driveway</a>… <a href='https://www.washingtonpost.com/lifestyle/2020/05/11/boy-5-steals-family-car-attempt-buy-lamborghini-then-man-with-lamborghini-shows-up-his-house/'>a five-year-old steals a car</a> to drive to LA to buy a Lamborghini, gets a free Lambo ride from Utah philanthropist… and Twitter <a href='https://twitter-com/DuckDuckGo/status/1255856182645919745'>think you’re interested in “egg”</a> and a bunch of other stuff besides, so share your lists with us on the Slack channel…
  • [00:15:35] <a href='https://twitter-com/ossia/status/1256340493027414019'>The .org registry is being confirmed to not be being sold</a>, <a href='https://twitter-com/timbray/status/1257326798565564421'>Tim Bray, VP, quits Amazon</a> over their firing of whistleblowers, and <a href='https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2020-05-06/facebook-recruits-elite-academics-lawyers-for-oversight-board'>Facebook creates an oversight board</a>, about which we are quietly pleased but a bit sceptical
  • [00:26:20] Our main piece: health and posture and wellness, both
digital and otherwise. Most of us in the technology community probably

need to do better at sitting up straight, positioning monitors correctly, standing up, exercising more, and so on. We’ve been taking a look at some of the tools to help accomplish this, from standing desks and posture monitors to education and putting your screen on a pile of books. This also dovetails with the drive towards digital wellness: after the big initiative a couple of years ago to have OS vendors build tools into their systems to help us switch off, did it work? What do the

tools do? And is anybody using them?

File:Bad Voltage 2x61 (IA badvoltage2x61.description:
Stuart Langridge, Jono Bacon, and Jeremy Garcia present Bad Voltage, in which a tenth of a point is more important than one might think it is, Mother Shipton is turning in her grave, and:


  • [00:02:10] <a href="https://www.badvoltage.org/2019/01/24/2x46/">A year ago</a>
we predicted everything that would happen in technology in 2019. Now…

we revisit those predictions and see how we did. No spoilers, but we will say: when we return in 2020 and give new predictions for the upcoming year… we’ll probably do better. File:Bad Voltage 2x63 (IA badvoltage2x63.author: Stuart Langridge, Jono Bacon
File:Bad Voltage 2x63 (IA badvoltage2x63.description:
Stuart Langridge, Jono Bacon, and special guest Jorge Castro present Bad Voltage, in which the nature of purchasing goods is discussed.

There seem to have recently been various examples of companies selling a thing and then exerting control over it after they’ve sold it. <a href="https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/technology-51206604">Sonos speakers have “recycle mode”</a>, HP printer cartridges in their “Instant Ink” programme <a href="https://twitter-com/danackerman/status/1218607344302596098">stop working if you unsubscribe</a>, and <a href="http://www.startribune.com/for-tech-weary-midwest-farmers-40-year-old-tractors-now-a-hot-commodity/566737082/">farmers buy 30-year-old tractors rather than new ones</a> because they’re still fixable in the field. But are these actually examples of a trend for the worse, or is this not actually the problem that it’s being painted as? Is this just how capitalism works, and is this how we want it to work? We’ll dive into this, from a few different perspectives, and see where we end up…

File:BachWards Prelude in C Major BWV846.author: TYalaA
File:BachWards Prelude in C Major BWV846.description: Backwards MIDI version of J S Bach [BWV 846] (c.1720) Prelude in C Major. Instead of the arpeggio being 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 3, 4, 5, this BachWards version uses 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 5, 4, 3. Of course, Bach's version was clever as playing 1, 2 at the start sets up the root key as this was originally for solo piano/ harpsichord. Playing it backwards means I had to add a double bass part to "cover up" the absence of the "root" at the start of each arpeggio. I also added an "ending bar" to loop the song (also because I'm only playing the first part of the Prelude). It is looped twice. I was intending the put the mp3 version here but mp3s aren't being accepted at the moment. You can hear the audio version at https://soundcloud.com/yahaya-abdullah/bachwards-prelude-in-c-major which is cool for elevators or telephone "on hold" music.

File:Cleanin' Up in Georgia by Harry P..author: Harry P. Guy
File:Cleanin' Up in Georgia by Harry P..description:
Original listing and sheet music here: https://musescore.com/user/36482158/scores/25050934?from=youtube_share 
"Cake Walk Patrol or Two-Step". A "Patrol" piece is one that simulates the point of view of an onlooker at a parade: the music is heard softly at first, then louder, then loud, then starts to soften again until it fades out in the distance. Harry P. Guy (1870-1950) was a talented composer and musician from Detroit who wrote this timeless piece in the year following his biggest hit, "Echoes from the Snowball Club". He was well known in the Detroit music scene for his music-making skills and bandleading and found time to write a stream of instrumentals and songs over several decades. This score was published by Willard Bryant in Detroit in 1899.

Original score source was from the book "Ragtime Rarities" by Trebor Jay Tichenor. A pdf copy can be found here: https://www.ceder.net/piano/viewsingle.php?Id=558&SqlId=1303156&style=thumb This is a reproduction of the original score.

Many thanks to JohnJ1995 of Musescore for requesting this classic cakewalk.

Harry P. Guy playlist: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLWv_HHmWjvjU-YjqSagXtaIaF3gTvUgHH

File:Clean boost before and after crunch.author: Skimel
File:Clean boost before and after crunch.description:
Clean boost after and before guitar amp on the edge of breakup.

When the boost is after the amp, only the volume increases. When the boost is before the amp, it pushes it into overdrive and the volume augmentation is less pronounced.

Gear used:

  • Guitar: Godin artisan ST (neck + bridge hotrail pickups)
  • amp and clean boost : Line 6 HX Stomp
    • amp: Cartographer (based on the Ben Adrian Cartographer), cab 4x12 Cartog Guv
    • Clean boost: boost provided by Kinky Comp (Xotic Sp Compressor emulation) with 0% mix (tone is not compressed at all, only the output is boosted)
    • Stereo plate reverb at the end of the chain.
Recorded in Reaper.

File:Day 0 Update -188 - E3 Wrap-Up (IA.author: SmashPad
File:Day 0 Update -188 - E3 Wrap-Up (IA.description:
On this episode of the Day 0 Update: Sony wants to ignore community concerns over Fortnite. Sky Skipper gets a release on the Nintendo Switch. Plus we wrap-up E3 with the games we saw that we cared about. 6/17/2018 - E3 Wrap-Up

  • Intro
  • What Are We Playing?
  • F: Sega Genesis Classics, Shaq Fu
  • P: Box Tetris with the occasional indulgence in Horizon Chase Turbo/SF 30th
  • B: Kingdom Hearts 1.5 + 2.5 Remix
  • C: Hitman Sniper Assassination, Fallout 4/Shelter, The Last of Us
  • D: A Hat in Time, Xbox Game Pass, Detroit: Become Human Platinum
  • <a href="https://www.forbes.com/sites/olliebarder/2018/06/14/arc-system-works-and-studio-trigger-are-collaborating-on-a-new-project-together/">Studio Trigger and Arc System Works bringing Kill La Kill to game systems</a>
  • <a href="https://www.polygon.com/e3/2018/6/14/17464550/donkey-kong-sky-skipper-arcade-archives-nintendo-switch">Donkey Kong & Sky Skipper coming to Nintendo Switch Arcade Archives</a>
  • D: Donkey Kong is actually available now and includes the original’s exploitable bugs.
  • <a href="https://www.polygon.com/2018/6/14/17463114/sony-ps4-fortnite-response-nintendo-switch-account">Sony responds to Fortnite account locks by not responding at all</a>
  • In other words, aw yeah fuck you, guys.
  • <a href="https://kotaku.com/fortnite-on-switch-has-built-in-voice-chat-no-app-requ-1826771335">Fortnite on the Switch has built-in voice chat, Switch app not needed</a>
  • <a href="https://steamed.kotaku.com/valve-adds-limits-to-steam-achievements-to-fight-rise-o-1826873740">Valve is adding limits to Steam Achievements to counter fake games</a>
  • <a href="https://kotaku.com/twitchs-e3-stream-punks-skate-4-fans-1826849076">Twitch trolled Skate fans with Skate 4 teaser bumper</a>
  • <a href="https://www.polygon.com/e3/2018/6/13/17460536/yoshi-nintendo-switch-release-date-delay">Nintendo’s Yoshi game for Switch was delayed to 2019</a>
  • D: While I don’t remember seeing that announcement, this and Fire Emblem are officially the first Switch delays.
  • <a href="https://kotaku.com/call-of-duty-fans-in-uproar-over-black-ops-4s-season-pa-1826788961">Activision is handling Black Ops 4’s season pass in the worst possible way</a>
  • <a href="https://www.gamasutra.com/view/news/319787/This_is_not_okay_EA_minces_no_words_on_backlash_against_women_in_Battlefield.php">EA’s Soderlund on Battlefield V women issue: “Either accept it or don’t buy the game.”</a>
  • <a href="http://www.newsweek.com/netflix-games-no-plans-get-gaming-service-977404">Netflix is sort of adding games to its service, Telltale is working on Stranger Things game</a>
  • Big E3 Sales on <a href="https://majornelson.com/2018/06/04/the-biggest-xbox-sale-of-the-year-drops-for-e3-week-including-50-off-xbox-one-x-and-much-more/">Xbox Live</a>, <a href="https://store.playstation.com/en-us/grid/STORE-MSF77008-BESTOFE3SALEGG/1?direction=asc&sort=name">PSN</a>, and <a href="https://www.nintendo.com/games/game-guide?pv=true#filter/-%7C-%7C-%7C-%7C-%7C-%7C-%7C-%7C-%7Ctrue%7C-%7C-%7C-%7C-%7Ctitle%7Casc%7C-%7C-">Nintendo eShop</a>
  • Games of E3
  • F: Doom Eternal, Tunic, Cyberpunk 2077, Trials Rising, Tetris Effect, Session
  • P: Fire Emblem: Three Houses, Octopath Traveler, Session, Anthem, Jupiter & Mars
  • B: Anthem, Cyberpunk 2077, Octopath Traveler, Ghost of Tsushima, Kingdom Hearts III
  • C: Hitman 2, Captain Spirit, Twin Mirror, Tetris Effect, Maneater, The Last of Us Part II, Just Cause 4, Afterparty, Ooblets
  • D: Tetris Effect, The Awesome Adventures of Captain Spirit , The Quiet Man, The Division 2, For Honor DLC, Overcooked 2, Killer Queen Black, Super Mario Party
  • E3 Closing Thoughts
  • Different, and sometimes disturbing approaches from each company.
  • P: Either they need to give up on E3 as an idea, or someone has to go old-school.
  • D: The E3 we grew up with, both as kids and industry analysts crafted in GameSpot’s prime, is dead and it’s probably not coming back.
  • All our unspoken rules are consistently broken.
  • The existence of Nintendo Directs and PSX don’t necessarily make it a totally bad thing.

    Subscribe via: <a href="https://itunes.apple.com/us/podcast/day-0-update/id991880432?mt=2">Apple Podcasts</a>, <a href="http://tunein.com/radio/Day-0-Update-p730071/">TuneIn</a>, <a href="https://goo-gl/app/playmusic?ibi=com.google.PlayMusic&isi=691797987&ius=googleplaymusic&link=https://play.google.com/music/m/I4y4y4lnjprhmetwvk7noevpw6i?t%3DDay_0_Update">Google Play</a>, or <a href="http://feeds.feedburner.com/Day0Update">RSS</a>

File:Cossypha humeralis, dagbreek-repert.author: JMK
File:Cossypha humeralis, dagbreek-repert.description:
Morning repertoire of a White-throated robin-chat, which delivers its song for some 15 minutes (12:25 included here) from the same perch in the upper branches of a bush clump with dense understory thicket, to which it could retreat for safety. It sings from 3-4 metres up in the open tree canopy, where it warms itself in the first rays of the morning sun. A second conspecific appears to answer from 2:40, right through, just within hearing distance. The original recording contains 138 phrases (the last 122 included in this clip), starting at 07:36 am and continuing for just over 14 minutes, i.e. a song phrase every 6 seconds. The sound graph suggests that the song is most vigorous soon after it starts, when perhaps the assumed male is most concerned with reestablishing his territory, and least vigorous in the last minute or so, when the sun is getting bright and other bird species noisier.

The recording was made late summer, and a northward migrating flock of European bee-eaters is audible from 8:30 in the clip, as they leave their night roost in a nearby tall Eucalypt. Additional background sounds are from Yellow-bellied greenbul (from 0:25), Black-headed oriole (1:10), Blue waxbill (1:40), Rock bunting (2:40), White-browed scrub robin (6:50), Cape turtle dove (from 7:13), Red-eyed dove (12:20) and Orange-breasted bushshrike, besides various scratching sounds when adjusting the recorder's cover, unfortunately.

The recording is from the centre of the Waterberg plateau, which is also at the centre of the species' range. A follow-up visit to the location at the start of June 2023 revealed no such morning repertoire at all, nor any perching at the top of trees. The song was replaced by less striking contact notes from the midst of thickets. This seems to be at odds with the Cape robin-chat, for instance, which sings vigorously at any time of the year.

File:Detection-of-Mouse-Cough-Based-on-S.author: Chen L, Lai K, Lomask J, Jiang B, Zhong N
File:Detection-of-Mouse-Cough-Based-on-S.description: According to the cough respiratory waveforms, we found the amplified sound waveforms. Noise 1 was the sound of head-twtich, the sound was similar to cough. But body movements were shaking head from left to right, which were different from raising head while coughing. Especially, the respiratory waveforms displayed “V” shape which was different from cough ones. Noise 2 was the sound of knocking chamber wall. When moving freely inside the plethysmograph, the mice may make sounds from frequent maneuvers such as nose-scratching, teeth-tapping, sniffing, et al. These sounds and body movements were so different from cough that could be distinguished by manipulator at real time. Otherwise, the noises produced different or no respiratory waveforms, and were thus well differentiated real-time from coughs using the Finepointe software.

File:Djuradj Vujcic Interviewing Arthur.author: Djuradj Vujcic
File:Djuradj Vujcic Interviewing Arthur.description:
An example of some of my early work.


Djuradj Vujcic: Tell me something about yourself. Where were you born, when...things like that.
Arthur Zaslavski: I was born in Belarus.
Djuradj Vujcic: What city?
Arthur Zaslavski: City is Brest, 1984, April 29th. I lived though in Estonia for seven years.
Djuradj Vujcic: Estonia?
Arthur Zaslavski: Yeah, I was only born in Belarus. Moved to Estonia, lived there til I was about eight. Moved here and now I'm twenty-three so most of my soccer has been basically brought up here.
Djuradj Vujcic: What team did you play for before?
Arthur Zaslavski: When I was younger I started here with Spartacus. My father was a coach – also coached professional in the Soviet Union and he taught me everything I know basically.
Other reporter: What's your dad's name?
Arthur Zaslavski: Pavel. Pavel Zaslavski. Yeah, he coached Zvezda. So yeah, everything that you see here, my skill, it's all been done basically 95% by my dad. There's been some outsiders here and there but the teams that I played for were Spartacus starting in '95. I was a striker. I started at the age of ten. At the age of thirteen, I switched to goalkeeper and from that point on, for ten years now, I've been playing goalkeeper.
Djuradj Vujcic: Who was your idol growing up? Lev Yashin?
Arthur Zaslavski: No, no (laughs). First, it was Peter Schmeichel but then after he retired it switched to Buffon.
Djuradj Vujcic: Did you, kind of, study them and...?
Arthur Zaslavski: No, not really. I didn't really study them too much but I just like Buffon especially because he started at the age of seventeen to play for Serie A, right – Parma. So that was kind of my inspiration because I also wanted to go pro at a young age.
Djuradj Vujcic: What do you think of the Serbian White Eagles – the team and the staff?
Arthur Zaslavski: Oh, I love it. It's a very good environment here. You know, everybody is friendly. They invited me here well so I feel like I'm part of the family now and I hope I'll have a good future here with the team.
Djuradj Vujcic: Alright, thanks.

Arthur Zaslavski: Yeah, no problem.

This is a small piece of educational sample for the demonstration of piano techniques, belonging to the session 'B22-B32 : Chou Chou's Slingshot shooting a Rotating force-tendency highway upwards

for enjoying a beautiful trip in the heavenly snow-land with Sun, Moon and Star-children shinning in the crystal universe together ' of one journal article researching Sir Debussy's Children's Corner - Doctor.

As one techniques-sample, it's tempo was expressively slowed down a little bit, but oppositely reflected out more emotional changes when watching impressions of binary system's progressing under background of CMB (Unbalanced balance surrounding hidden gravitational axis - turning round and turning back - waving by waving). Meanwhile, you can also hear the parts of deep self-reasoning and down-falling towards clouds. I thought basic principles of impressionism, according to Sir Debussy's notation-transcript, had been kept. Better edition based on classroom background, will be researched out for commons' free shares and usages .

File:Drums opening and closing a noise g.author: Skimel
File:Drums opening and closing a noise g.description:
Exemple audio d'un noise gate appliqué sur un pad de synthé et dont l'ouverture est déclenchée par une batterie.

On entend d'abord le pad de synthé seul, puis la batterie seule, et ensuite les deux instruments ensemble. Ensuite, le noise gate est activé, produisant un son haché. Enfin, on entend le synthé seul avec le noise gate, pour bien entendre l'effet.

Réalisé dans Reaper avec les VST suivants :

  • Synthé : Surge (MKS 70 Warm Pad) - accord de Do majeur joué en midi
  • Batterie : addictive Drums 2, kit "Retroplex Eighties Box", pattern "909 techno"
  • Noise gate : ReaGate
    • attack : 50 ms
    • Hold : 10 ms
    • Release : 100 ms
La grosse caisse et le charley de la batterie (kick et hi-hat) sont envoyés dans l'entrée auxiliaire du gate (sidechain), et déclenchent son ouverture. Ainsi, le son du synthé n'est joué que lorske le kick ou le hit hat sont joués.

File:Fearless First (ISRC USUAN1600058)..author: Kevin MacLeod
File:Fearless First (ISRC USUAN1600058)..description:
Fearless First
Before you complain about the bass, that is the entire point of this mix. It is scary-bass... yet somehow subdued. If this bass was a car, it would be a cement mixer... That's a terrible analogy. Forgetting for the moment that a cement mixer isn't a car... I guess they have the ones that are mounted on big trucks - and those trucks share a lot in common with cars, you know steering wheels, engines, tires, and the soon-to-be-anachronistic internal combustion engine. Anyway, if you don't like the bass you can pretty easily EQ it to a reasonable level, or buy the stems and remix it yourownself. Before you complain about the use of the word "yourownself", I wrote it. You understood it. It is a word. There is also some dreamy flute in here.

File:Ethan Hein - 01 - Departure Store d.author: Ethan Hein
File:Ethan Hein - 01 - Departure Store d.description:
Departure Store (disquiet0043-dazzledmachine) by Ethan Hein.
For this week's Junto, the goal was to take pre-existing field recordings and to turn them into something else. The pre-existing field recordings are the audio produced by Disquiet Junto members for projects 0037 and 0038. Here are the two I used: Ascension: Macy's Escalator [disquiet0037-asrealasitgets1] by Super Miracle Dream Team Post [disquiet0037-asrealasitgets1] by Lem Herlihy The field recordings in question are documents of retail spaces, such department stores. We were told to rework the audio from one or more of the field recordings to achieve something inspired by the following description: "There was the continuous roar of the machine at work, of customers crowding into the departments, dazzled by the merchandise, then propelled towards the cash-desk. And it was all regulated and organized with the remorselessness of a machine: the vast horde of women were as if caught in the wheels of an inevitable force." The quote comes from the novel Au Bonheur des Dames, or The Ladies' Paradise, by Émile Zola, originally published in 1883. I found the more rhythmically and texturally interesting elements in the two recordings, mostly sounds of escalators and a forklift backing up. Some muzak also found its way in. I used my entire bag of Ableton tricks to impose beats and tonality. File:HWHAP Ep407 A Place in Space to Cal.author: NASA Johnson Space Center
File:HWHAP Ep407 A Place in Space to Cal.description: Nilufar Ramji Houston We Have a Podcast. Welcome to the official podcast of the NASA Johnson Space Center, Episode 407: A Place in Space to Call Home, Part 1. I'm Nilufar Ramji, and I'll be your host today. On this podcast, we bring in the experts, scientists, engineers, and astronauts, all to let you know what's going on in the world of human spaceflight and more. For the last 25 years, humans have lived and worked aboard the International Space Station… turning what was once a dream into a permanent home in space. What started as a bold idea has grown into a symbol of international cooperation, a cutting-edge orbiting laboratory and a launch pad for humanity's future exploration of the Moon, Mars, and beyond. For the astronauts who have lived aboard the space station for these 25 years, the experience of calling the space station home has looked a little different for each one. As part of our ISS25 series, we had the opportunity to speak with two NASA astronauts who each have different perspectives of life on the space station. You'll be hearing from one of them, Tracy Dyson, on this episode; and coming soon in Part 2, Mark Vande Hei will tell us about his experiences in space. Tracy Dyson's career is deeply tied to the history of the International Space Station, from helping to assemble it aboard the Space Shuttle Endeavor on STS-118 in 2007, to living and working there in 2010 during expeditions 23 and 24 and most recently, returning for expeditions 70 and 71 in 2024. We'll reflect on what it means to celebrate 25 years of continuous human presence in space, what life aboard the space station is really like, and how this orbiting outpost is preparing us for the next great era of exploration. Here's Tracy Dyson. Nilufar Ramji Tracy, welcome to Houston We Have a Podcast. We are so happy to have you here. Tracy Dyson Thank you. It's my pleasure. Nilufar Ramji So before we get into the topic of the space station, I want our listeners to get to know you. So tell us a little bit about you, your background, and maybe when you joined NASA, what what things were like at that time? What was human space flight exploration looking like at that time? Tracy Dyson I should go back to the the year of 1997 I had finished up my PhD and submitted my dissertation in the month of June, and I think it was the next month July, when I submitted my application for the astronaut program. And then I went on and did a postdoctoral fellow fellow fellowship in Southern California at UC Irvine. And it was during that period of time that I got the notice to that I was being offered an interview. And so that start that kicked it off. And and then later on that year, I was selected in August of 1998, just prior to turning- my birthday, in fact. And so I began in 1998 with the class group 17. We were called the Penguins, and we were not the largest class, but probably the second largest class of astronauts, with or without our international partner astronauts, we were 25 altogether. Nilufar Ramji Wow. Tracy Dyson Yeah, there was big but the group before us, the sardines, as they were called, had something like 44 so it was a huge, huge astronaut corps when we arrived. And there's, you know, depending on which astronauts you asked, there was somewhere between 110 to 140 astronauts. I mean, it wherever it fell, at any one given time, there was a lot of astronauts during that period of time. And it was also a transition time where we were flying shuttles for individual missions, but transitioning to building the International Space Station. And so we, we the class of 1998 are kind of the babies of the International Space Station, because it was only a couple months after our arrival, while we were still astronaut candidates, that we launched the first element of the International Space Station, the functional cargo block. Nilufar Ramji That is really exciting. No one can see me right now. I'm smiling ear to ear, just because you actually helped build the space station. You put it together. Yeah, and it's been up there for 25 years. Tell us a little bit about what that was like. Tracy Dyson Oh gosh, it's hard to put it in a nutshell, because there were so many facets of the construction of the space station. I mean, for us to have a space station, first of all, brand new idea. I mean, minus all the time it took to conceive the idea, plan it, and do all. Work to get the elements but But nevertheless, the operations of an International Space Station were in its complete infancy, and we were a long way from where we are today in terms of even knowing how we were going to operate, because each and every shuttle flight was bringing up a new element to the space station. Each and every flight meant that the configuration of the space station was changing. And so as new astronauts, here we are learning everything. We had to learn about the space shuttle, which was delivering everything, and then we had to learn about each piece of international space station all by itself, and then what it was going to be like when it joined the existing station as we were building it. And at the time- and you ask anybody who was around during that period of time, it was every every shuttle flight was a brand new schematic. Every procedure had a number associated with it, depending on what flight it was. The NBL- the NBL had different mock ups and different configurations and different space walk teams depending on what the configuration of the space station was. And so talk about flexibility and adaptability, right? It was 100% required during the assembly of the International Space Station. Nilufar Ramji I just what an exciting time to be at the agency! A period of change, evolution, growth, so many things happening. Tracy Dyson Absolutely, and you want to know that the hard truth is that when we arrived, NASA was not the brand everybody was wearing. In fact, as we transitioned into this International Space Station, the country was a bit skeptical about the money that we were spending as taxpayers on this notion of a space station, and what, what was it going to do for us, and we as astronauts, were, you know, the face out there. And we had to not only learn the technical details and the operational concepts and stuff that we were developing, but we also had to talk about the science, which we had not even done yet. I mean, we were building a laboratory. We weren't actually functioning in one yet, right? But yet, we had to forecast what, what it was going to look like, and be able to communicate it and convince folks that this is the right thing to do. And luckily, It withstood the test of time, but it was really a hard period of time. It's not the kind of excitement that we enjoy today. Today's Space Station is a proven platform, and everybody's like, wants to be a part of it from around the world. But back when we first started, it was tough. Nilufar Ramji It's always hard to build that foundation for everyone to understand what the, you know, the 5, 10, 25-year plan is. So it's exciting that you got to be there in the assembly, and then you made another trip later on where you saw it fully assembled, and it was living and working aboard that so that proven- that, that proving ground that you established in the early years, you got to live it out in the same time, right? Tracy Dyson Yes, yeah, I would say that my flights were placed in such a way that gave me such a view to what we have today. And my my shuttle flight was just a dear time in my life for lots of reasons. But as far as the assembly goes, we brought up an element. And even though it was, you know, by comparison to other elements quite small, was the S5, the Starboard 5 truss. And if you looked at a model of the space station today or a picture of it, you'd be hard pressed to pick out where that thing is, but it is a necessary spacer between two sets of solar arrays. So just want to get that out there. But nevertheless, we did some other things on that flight that were significant, but we were just a part of the assembly and and so that, with with that objective, we docked to the space station for a period of time. And so I got to see what life was like on board without being an Expedition crew member. I just got to live on board the shuttle, go in there, do our work, come back out, etc, for 10 glorious, docked days of a 12, almost 13 day mission. And then when I came back as an Expedition crew member, I was right at that, that cusp of assembly complete. And, you know, full fledged utilization is what we'd say. But, but we weren't quite full fledged yet, we were aspiring utilization, and so we were at the point where the station wasn't going to grow anymore in terms of the number of modules and everything like that. But we were, we were starting to figure out, how are we going to be now efficient with our operations? How are we now going to focus turn our focus from building this thing to actually using it. And so it was really an interesting time, as we it was clunky, very, very clunky in in, in retrospect right now, and the time, it was just like chaos, but, you know, not really sure how it was going to take shape. And then, most recently, I went up. You know, 14 years later, and there's been a lot of changes, not to the structure of the space station, but to the operations, the mindset and the slick products and concepts that we have that have allowed us to do some of the most groundbreaking, sophisticated science on or off the planet. Nilufar Ramji I have so many questions, but I want to take a pause for a quick second and ask you one specific thing. Tracy Dyson Sure. Nilufar Ramji It's been 25 years of the space station. Can you give us a little bit of your reflections of what the last 25 years have been like when you're looking at the space station, and literally you did everything from assemble it, look at process improvement. You've gone up there in different phases of what, what is the space station today? So I want to hear a little bit about your reflections on that. Tracy Dyson I gotta pick… Nilufar Ramji Is there a certain feeling you might get? Like, are you feeling really proud because you're smiling with us right now? Tracy Dyson Well, pride is one part of it. I don't want to get emotional, but I feel like, I, you know, when I, when I joined NASA, I felt like a full fledged adult. File:Inleiding Gr\u00e4we-Reijseger-Hemi.author: deSingel
File:Inleiding Gr\u00e4we-Reijseger-Hemi.description: Wide awake, on the edge of your seat. This is how you'll be listening to Georg Gräwe, Ernst Reijseger and Gerry Hemingway. They search together for sounds without a clear alpha and omega. Playfully, with combinations of materials and techniques, the trio spirits away any difference between composition and improvisation using differently coloured layers of sound. Tradition and innovation are virtually indistinguishable. Free improvisation was the trio's starting point when they began working together in 1989. Twenty years later these three alert musicians switch effortlessly from tautly composed parts to totally free passages. Their adventurous story succeeds in gripping us time and time again, right down to the last note. The trio continues to find openings and cracks in the dense music through which to fire off unforeseen accents with a subtle, virtually unnoticeable irony. They gently undermine faultlessly built-up, tense expectations. This music does not tolerate a single moment of rest. Up to you to enjoy it to the full.

File:Inleiding An Index Of Memories (aud.author: deSingel
File:Inleiding An Index Of Memories (aud.description: He and She, each with their own memories in two different worlds. Will they get on the same wavelength? She is experiencing intensely emotional Sapphic poetry, reminisces, talks about desire. He is at a turning point. His words are no more than scraps of memory strung together; he rewrites the past. Her language is narrative, like the memory of the ancient civilisation of the West. His language falters, it is the language of the memory of the modern age. 'An Index of Memories' is a scenic concert on memory and its emotions. It is all based on the writings left us by the ancient Greek poetess Sappho. Love, erotic desire and the hope it expresses are emotional memories of all ages. Annelies Van Parys had already set several of Sappho's poems to music. They form the starting point for a full-length composition in which past and present come into contact and complement each other. Caroline Petrick stretches the concept of the 'scenic concert' to the limit. Somewhere between scene and concert, space and the absence of it, and between index and memory, she seeks out a way in which music can be conceived.

File:Inleiding Richard Goode (audio) 264.author: deSingel
File:Inleiding Richard Goode (audio) 264.description: Richard Goode is back! We had to miss him for a while, as he had taken a sabbatical. That was not to idle his time away, but to recharge and explore new repertoire. And it is with renewed energy and undoubtedly further matured insights that he returns to his great love, Beethoven, and not least to the holy trinity of the piano repertoire, the master's last three sonatas. This is a 'tour de force' by any standards, since they demand the utmost from the performer. They are, indeed, a synthesis of all the forms and ways of expression that Beethoven had explored in the preceding sonatas. For the performer, it is a tremendous challenge to find the right balance between the many opposites - between intimate reverie and explosive eruption, between complex fugue and simple aria, between the mundane and the exalted, all the expression of a rich personality. But by no means beyond this great pianist.

File:Inleiding Trio Moore - Phillips - P.author: deSingel
File:Inleiding Trio Moore - Phillips - P.description: Give Michael Moore a free hand and you're bound to get something very special. He is never boring and always surprises. He and his partners lead you on a seemingly unending voyage of discovery through a succession of atmospheric excursions and impressions. We are talking jazz, but the definition 'atmospheric music with improvisation' will probably grab your imagination more. There is variation from bustle and storm to calm and reflection. Sounds are placed in space like specks of paint in a pointillist painting, which Barre Phillips himself describes as 'putting sound objects in space'. A musical sparring match with a whole range of colours and effects in combination with body sounds. The melodic percussion of Pallemaerts, the eye-catcher in this trio, drives the music more in lyrical terms than in rhythmic. The other musicians, too, use few notes. Moore's themes convince and stick, and he is able to make melodies speak as no other. The trio is masterly in mixing various influences and experiences to bring about highly dynamic and exciting jazz adventures. In Josse De Pauw's words, 'Listening to Moore is to witness the changing of the seasons'.

File:Inleiding BOHO Strings olv. David R.author: deSingel
File:Inleiding BOHO Strings olv. David R.description: “The most horrific period in history has finally come to an end”, wrote Richard Strauss at the end of World War II. The ‘Metamorphosen’, composed during the darkest days, are his personal reflection on the total destruction that resulted from the war. From a musical point of view, this work marks a turning point: we are not used to such dark and above all intimate sound combinations from him.Intense, raw emotions also play a central role in Raminta Serksnyte’s work. ‘De Profundis’ combined the post-romantic tragedy of Strauss with the sound worlds of jazz, minimalism and the avant-garde. In the music of Wim Henderickx and Vladimir Martynov, the Grim Reaper is lurking just around the corner, which for them is an opportunity for meditation and silence.Reflections on life and death that will leave no one unmoved.At this concert Boho Strings will also present its first CD - 'Nostalgia' - released by Antarctica Records, and entirely dedicated to the music of Belgian composer Wim Henderickx. Please join artistic director David Ramael and Wim Henderickx after the concert for an exclusive signing session.

File:Korg Volca Keys polyphonic behaviou.author: Attosaur
File:Korg Volca Keys polyphonic behaviou.description:
Artificial simulation of how we'd expect the Korg Volca Keys synth heard in this file to sound if it wasn't paraphonic (i.e. if it had a separate envelope generator (EG) for each voice).

The behaviour here is more natural, like (e.g.) a piano or most modern synths. While you can hear previous notes continue to play at a low level, they aren't unnaturally "brought back" at full volume.

Demo created by layering three notes played completely separately in editing software. (A real Volca Keys could not reproduce this on its own- that's the entire point.)

File:Male bellbird 01.ogg.description: Male Bellbird vocalising at intervals of 20 to 30 seconds.  The bird is constantly turning its head apparently listening and watching then extends its whole body to emit each loud note. Distant background bird calls are from Hihi, Blackbird, Greywarbler, and Kaka.  Sequence ends with the "whirr" of the Bellbird's wings as it flys off. Recorded near birdfeeders in the "Discovery area", Karori wildlife sanctuary (Zealandia), Wellington, New Zealand.

File:Marco Kalnenek - 122 - ElectricShoc.author: Marco Kalnenek
File:Marco Kalnenek - 122 - ElectricShoc.description:
ElectricShockingKrautRockingMinimalMachine by Marco Kalnenek. Marco Kalnenek [*1969] is a musician from Heerlen, the Netherlands.

Kalnenek started playing the piano at age 9. His first band Foolish Behaviour was formed around 1982, when he started jamming and recording tapes with assorted friends. Hundreds of hours of music and other noises were recorded in the 12 years that followed. A few cassettes and cd-r’s were privately released and various tracks turned up on compilations, most notably on Comfort Stand Recordings and blocSonic. In the meantime Kalnenek started his own label, WM Recordings, in 2004.

After years of relative inactivity Marco Kalnenek’s first official EP “If Not For” finally appeared in May 2013.

File:Lift Up Your Hearts (Woodlands tune.author: Melody: Walter Greatorex (1877-1949); setting & sound file: Rabanus Flavus (Peter Gerloff)
File:Lift Up Your Hearts (Woodlands tune.description:
Lift up your hearts (Woodlands tune)

'Lift up your hearts!' We lift them, Lord, to thee;
Here at thy feet none other may we see:
'Lift up your hearts!' E'en so, with one accord,
We lift them up, we lift them to the Lord.

Above the level of the former years,
The mire of sin, the slough of guilty fears,
The mist of doubt, the blight of love's decay,
O Lord of Light, lift all our hearts to-day!

Above the swamps of subterfuge and shame,
The deeds, the thoughts, that honor may not name,
The halting tongue that dares not tell the whole,
O Lord of Truth, lift every Christian soul!

Lift every gift that thou thyself hast given;
Low lies the best till lifted up to heaven:
Low lie the bounding heart, the teeming brain,
Till, sent from God, they mount to God again.

Then, as the trumpet-call, in after years,
'Lift up your hearts!' rings pealing in our ears,
Still shall those hearts respond, with full accord,
'We lift them up, we lift them to the Lord!'
